history.summary: CSV town corrected from Purulia to Para (the village is ~28-30 km northeast of Purulia town, on the route to Banda Deul). Historical records suggest Para may have served as the capital of the Panchakot kings and possibly earlier of the Manrajas. Three weathered deul temples survive: (1) a 40-ft stone temple, likely predating the others, with clear Odisha influence - its stonework of dancing figures and floral motifs has largely eroded, and local Jain-community tradition is credited with its construction; (2) a 45-ft brick temple of the 10th-11th century (estimate; top collapsed) with fine decorative brickwork, closely resembling the Deulghata deuls, whose interior houses an obliterated circular sculpture locally known as Udaychandi and worshipped every Tuesday; (3) a smaller, much more dilapidated mixed stone-and-brick temple on the village's western edge. The temples are mainly Brahmanical with strong Jain influence, typical of Purulia's plateau sites. Coordinates are street-level from the map geocoder (Sarak Para Road, Raghunathpur), so they are approximate to the village rather than exact.

name: Para Temples
town_description: Para is a small village in Purulia district, about 28-30 km northeast of Purulia town on the route to the Banda Deul in the Raghunathpur area. It was probably a royal capital in medieval times but is now a quiet agricultural settlement; visitors come for the three ancient deuls and continue to Banda, Cheliyama and the Ajodhya Hills circuit.
